prompt: In a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle the hypotenuse is $12$. How long is the short leg, the one opposite the $30^\circ$ angle?
explanation: In a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle, the side opposite $30^\circ$ is always HALF the hypotenuse.

alternativeExplanations.title: Cut a triangle in half
steps: Take an equilateral triangle with all sides $12$ and slice it straight down the middle.
Each half is a $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle, and the bottom edge of $12$ got cut into two $6$s.

alternativeExplanations.title: Use the memorized ratio
steps: A $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle has sides in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$.
The hypotenuse matches the $2$, so $2$ parts $= 12$ and $1$ part $= 6$.
The short leg is $1$ part, so it is $6$.
